If you miss a payment, your account is not disconnected right away. Here's how it works, based on the knowledge base:

- **45 days past due:** The account is flagged for a service review. [Billing & Account FAQs > What happens if I miss a payment?]
- **90 days past due:** Disconnection for non-payment applies only to non-payment exceeding 90 days. [Billing & Account FAQs > What happens if I miss a payment?]
- **Billing disputes:** SunGrid does not disconnect community-tier members from shared array access over billing disputes. [Billing & Account FAQs > What happens if I miss a payment?]

**If an autopay charge fails** (for example, insufficient funds or an expired card):

- SunGrid retries the charge twice more over the following 5 business days. If the retries fail, the account switches to manual-pay for that billing cycle. [Autopay Failure & Retry Policy > What Happens When Autopay Fails?]
- You'll get an email and a portal notification after the first failed attempt, with instructions to update your payment method. A second notification is sent if the retry also fails. [Autopay Failure & Retry Policy > Notifications]
- Late-payment timelines still apply and are counted from the original due date, not from the date autopay failed. [Autopay Failure & Retry Policy > Relationship to Late Payment Policy]

**To fix it:** You can re-enroll in autopay anytime in the member portal under Account Settings. Re-enrollment takes effect on the next billing cycle. [Autopay Failure & Retry Policy > Re-Enrolling in Autopay]

Your autopay charge failed because your card expired. Here's what happens next:

1. **Retries:** SunGrid retries the charge twice more over the following 5 business days [Autopay Failure & Retry Policy > What Happens When Autopay Fails?].

4. **Late-payment timelines:** The standard 45-day and 90-day late-payment timelines still apply. They are counted from the original due date, not from the date autopay failed [Autopay Failure & Retry Policy > Relationship to Late Payment Policy].

**To fix it:** Update your payment method and re-enroll in autopay through the member portal under Account Settings. Re-enrollment takes effect on the next billing cycle, so this cycle's payment may still need to be made manually [Autopay Failure & Retry Policy > Re-Enrolling in Autopay].

The Rooftop Rebate Program has these eligibility rules:

- **Household tier:** Applies to Household-tier members installing a new rooftop system.
- **System size:** Must be between 3 kW and 10 kW. This is a hard requirement.
- **Service region:** The household must be within the SunGrid service region, as listed on the approved ZIP code list (Appendix A).
- **Income:** Household adjusted gross income must fall below the regional threshold that the Cooperative Board publishes annually. This is also a hard requirement.
- **Installer:** Systems installed by non-approved installers are not eligible, regardless of other criteria.

The program runs on a rolling annual budget. If the budget is used up, new applications go on a waitlist until the next fiscal year's budget is released. [Incentive & Rebate Programs > Program Funding Status]

Your extra charge is most likely a **rebate recovery adjustment**. This happens when a previously approved rooftop rebate is reversed because an eligibility error was found after the payment was made. Examples include an installer later found not to be on the approved list, or a household later found to exceed the income threshold. SunGrid then recovers the disbursed amount through your bills. [Rebate Refund & Billing Adjustment Notice > Overview] [Rebate Refund & Billing Adjustment Notice > Reversal Process]

**Why it's spread over several bills:** The adjustment is applied over up to 6 monthly billing cycles rather than as one lump charge, to reduce hardship on the household. [Rebate Refund & Billing Adjustment Notice > Reversal Process]

**Who is responsible:** The Incentive Program committee makes the reversal determination, and the Billing team carries out the adjustment schedule. [Rebate Refund & Billing Adjustment Notice > Which Team Handles This?]

**Notice and appeal:**
- You should have received written notice at least 30 days before the first adjusted billing cycle. [Rebate Refund & Billing Adjustment Notice > Member Notification]
- You can appeal the reversal through the Incentive Program appeals process in the Incentive & Rebate Programs document. The general member grievance procedure does not apply to this. [Rebate Refund & Billing Adjustment Notice > Member Notification]

**How it's paid:**
- **Autopay:** The adjustment is applied automatically to your scheduled charge. [Rebate Refund & Billing Adjustment Notice > Interaction with Autopay]
- **Manual payment:** You must acknowledge the revised amount in the member portal before the next billing cycle. If a payment fails, the autopay-failure handling process in the Billing & Account FAQs applies. [Rebate Refund & Billing Adjustment Notice > Interaction with Autopay]
